summary.tldr: Creates an ombud office to review Citizenship and Immigration practices, take complaints, make recommendations, and report to Parliament.
what_it_does: Creates the Office of the Ombud for the Department of Citizenship and Immigration and sets a seven-year appointment process for the ombud, with approval by the Senate and House of Commons.

Gives the ombud power to examine whether the department’s practices are fair, equitable, unbiased, non-racist and non-discriminatory, including in decisions under the Citizenship Act and the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act.
Lets any person file a complaint and allows the ombud to investigate on their own, at the minister’s request, or after a complaint, with powers to summon witnesses, require records and take evidence.
Requires the ombud to send reports to the minister and complainant, and requires the minister to reply with steps taken or reasons for not following recommendations.
Adds the ombud to the Language Skills Act and makes related changes to access to information, privacy, financial administration, superannuation and compensation laws.
Requires annual reports, allows special reports, and sets a parliamentary review of the Act every five years after it comes into force.
who_it_affects: People dealing with Citizenship and Immigration
summary.background: The bill says the new office would review the department’s practices and investigate unfairness, bias, racism and discrimination in its decision-making. It would not review matters that happened before the office was created unless the minister asks.
